answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may earn reputation or enter high-value tasks. A verifier samples completed work and, after a challenge period, slashes the bond for provable fraud; honest agents recover it. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and cheating risks losing it, so scaling a sybil attack becomes costly rather than free. The bond might be denominated in walnut credits, with orchard and basalt used as task labels—not as evidence of identity.
